Well, it's April now and time to get the stevia in the ground. I've been doing this on my 1.1 mu for about 15 years — switched from wheat because the grain price was always terrible and at least the stevia buyer comes to the village. My son and his wife work at a factory in the county town, so this land is mostly me and my wife's business now. We need the cash for daily costs and my granddaughter's school fees, but every yuan I spend has to come from somewhere.

I always buy seedlings from the nursery down the road. I need about 9,000 plants for my plot — one big bundle and a smaller one — and that costs around 650 yuan. It's a lot of money to pay all at once. Last year I thought about trying to grow my own seedlings to save cash, but I don't have the greenhouse space and the nursery plants just grow better. My neighbor Old Zhang tried saving his own and they were weak. So I pay.

For the soil, I hire Old Wang to bring his rotary tiller around mid-April, costs me 55 yuan. Then before planting I spread about one and a half bags of that 15-15-15 compound fertilizer — that's roughly 75 kg per mu. I also throw down whatever chicken manure I've got from our backyard coop, maybe half a cartload. I don't know exactly how much, maybe 200-300 jin. I used to put two bags of compound on, but fertilizer got expensive last year, and I noticed Old Li cut back and his crop was fine. So I'm trying less this year. I've still got some urea in the shed from last year; if the leaves look yellow in June, I'll sprinkle maybe 5 kg per mu. But I'm not buying new urea unless I have to.

I irrigate five times from the well. Flood irrigation across the border, same as I've always done. The electric pump costs about 8 yuan each time for electricity. I'll water right after planting, then twice when the heat comes in June and July, and twice more before harvest in late August. We had a dry spring two years ago and I learned my lesson. But my wife complains every time the electricity bill comes, so I don't water more than I need.

For weeds, I spray herbicide once right after planting. Me and my wife also hand-weed once in July — takes us two days bending over in the sun. My back isn't what it used to be, but hiring someone costs 80 yuan a day, and I can't pay that for weeding. For bugs, I keep a small bottle of insecticide in the shed and only spray if I see damage. Last July there were some caterpillars, so I sprayed twice. I don't bother with fungicide — never had a problem bad enough to spend money on.

Planting the seedlings takes me and my wife three full days of kneeling and planting by hand. Harvest is in late August or early September, depending on when the leaves look right. That's another week of hard work. If my back is acting up like it did last year, I might hire one person for two days to help with the cutting. But I'd rather do it myself and save the 160 yuan.

I think I'll get about 400 kg per mu this year. Last year was only 380 because of that dry June. The buyer pays about 4 yuan per kg for the fresh leaves, so if I'm lucky I'll get around 1,800 yuan total. After the seedlings, fertilizer, irrigation, tilling, and the chemicals, maybe 900 yuan is gone. It doesn't leave much, but what else can you do with 1.1 mu? At least I know stevia.
